finding_en: Biotite from a sheared orthogneiss in the Three Pagodas Fault Zone at Khao Chon Kai, NW of Kanchanaburi, gave a 40Ar/39Ar plateau age of 33.4 ± 0.3 Ma. The authors interpret it as the end of ductile left-lateral shear during India-driven extrusion of Indochina in the late Eocene–early Oligocene.
value: 40Ar/39Ar biotite plateau 33.4 ± 0.3 Ma (sample TL21)

site.name_th: เขาชนไก่ อำเภอเมืองกาญจนบุรี (เขตรอยเลื่อนเจดีย์สามองค์)
site.name_en: Khao Chon Kai, Three Pagodas Fault Zone, NW of Kanchanaburi

citation.text: Lacassin, Maluski, Leloup, Tapponnier, Hinthong, Siribhakdi, Chuaviroj & Charoenravat 1997, Tertiary diachronic extrusion and deformation of western Indochina, Journal of Geophysical Research 102(B5):10013–10037

_notes: DOI confirmed on Crossref (JGR Solid Earth 102(B5):10013-10037, 10 May 1997). I read the FULL TEXT (the author's PDF from ipgp.fr, converted to text). Exact statements: 'An orthogneiss sample has been taken at Khao Chon Kai (99°24'-14°08'N), NW of Kanchanaburi within the Three Pagodas fault zone (TL21, Figure 1b).' Table 1: 'TL21 biotite plateau 33.4 ± 0.3, total 32.7 ± 0.8, isochron (32.6 ± 0.5)'. Text: 'A biotite age of 33.4 ± 0.3 Ma has been obtained in the sample TL21 from the Three Pagodas fault zone... we interpret this age as the age of terminal left-lateral shear along that zone. This is also in line with the previous K/Ar dating results (36 ± 1 Ma, 33 ± 2 Ma...)' (K–Ar on Thabsila gneisses, Bunopas 1981), 'possibly implying that shear lasted at least from 36 and 33 Ma B.P.' The paper also says 'a lowermost Oligocene age deformation (36 to 33 Ma)' for the Three Pagodas zone, and that ductile shear on the Wang Chao (Mae Ping) zone ended at about 30.5 Ma. Coordinates are converted from 99°24'E, 14°08'N, precision about 1'. The paper also notes that present-day slip senses are opposite to the finite geological offsets, which supports the separate 'fault-reversal' event, though that reversal is not dated here.

title_th: อายุ K–Ar ของหินบะซอลต์บ่อพลอย
title_en: K–Ar age of the Bo Phloi basalt
finding_th: การหาอายุด้วยวิธีโพแทสเซียม–อาร์กอน (K–Ar) ของหินบะซอลต์แอลคาไลที่บ่อพลอย จังหวัดกาญจนบุรี ให้อายุ 3.14 ± 0.17 ล้านปี (สมัยไพลโอซีน) ซึ่งเป็นช่วงที่ลาวานำแร่คอรันดัม (ไพลินและบุษราคัม) ขึ้นมาสู่ผิวโลก
finding_en: K–Ar dating of the alkali basalt at Bo Phloi, Kanchanaburi, gave 3.14 ± 0.17 Ma (Pliocene), the eruption that brought sapphire-bearing corundum to the surface.

citation.text: Barr & Macdonald 1981, Geochemistry and geochronology of late Cenozoic basalts of Southeast Asia, GSA Bulletin 92(8, Part II):1069–1142

_notes: DOI confirmed on Crossref (GSA Bull. 92(8 Part II):1069-1142, Aug 1981). The companion Part I summary is doi:10.1130/0016-7606(1981)92<508:GAGOLC>2.0.CO;2 (GSA Bull. 92:508). I did NOT read either paper. The value 3.14 ± 0.17 Ma (K–Ar) for Bo Phloi, attributed to Barr & Macdonald 1981, is repeated in secondary sources seen as search snippets (a GIT/Khamloet et al. document on sapphire inclusions, and Mindat). The same snippets cite an 40Ar/39Ar age of 4.17 ± 0.11 Ma from 'Sutthirat et al., 1994', for which I found no verifiable publication. Sutthirat et al. 2020 (J. Asian Earth Sci. 187:104068; abstract read) refers to the '~4–3 Ma ages of the Bo Phloi basalt'. The timeline's 3.14 Ma matches this K–Ar value. Please check the sample table in Barr & Macdonald Part II (it may spell the site 'Bo Ploi'). Site is null because no coordinates were given in a source I read.

title_th: อายุ U–Pb เซอร์คอนในไพลินและกรวดบ่อพลอย
title_en: Zircon U–Pb ages in Bo Phloi sapphires
finding_th: เซอร์คอนที่เป็นมลทิน (inclusion) ในไพลิน และเซอร์คอนจากชั้นกรวดที่มีไพลินสองแหล่งที่บ่อพลอย ให้อายุ U–Pb เฉลี่ย 24 ± 0.9, 10.86 ± 0.14 และ 4.4 ± 0.4 ล้านปี ซึ่งเก่ากว่าหินบะซอลต์บ่อพลอย (~4–3 ล้านปี) แสดงว่าไพลินตกผลึกในเปลือกโลกตอนล่างเป็นระยะ ๆ ก่อน แล้วหินบะซอลต์จึงพาขึ้นมาภายหลัง
finding_en: A zircon inclusion in sapphire and zircons from two sapphire-bearing gravels at Bo Phloi gave mean U–Pb ages of 24 ± 0.9, 10.86 ± 0.14 and 4.4 ± 0.4 Ma. These are older than the ~4–3 Ma Bo Phloi basalt, so the sapphires crystallised episodically at depth and were later carried up by the basalt.

citation.text: Sutthirat, Pisutha-Arnond, Khamloet & Assawincharoenkij 2020, Multistages of original sapphire formation related to basaltic magmatism in the Bo Phloi basaltic gem field, Journal of Asian Earth Sciences 187:104068

_notes: DOI confirmed on Crossref (J. Asian Earth Sci. 187, article 104068, Jan 2020). Read the full abstract via the Semantic Scholar API. Quote: 'The U-Pb dating of a zircon inclusion in sapphire and zircons in two sapphire-bearing gravels yielded the average ages of 24 ± 0.9, 10.86 ± 0.14 and 4.4 ± 0.4 Ma, respectively... These ages are, however, mostly pre-dated (one is close to) ~4–3 Ma ages of the Bo Phloi basalt... the formation of sapphire... occurred episodically earlier during ~24–4 Ma... Later, the eruption of mantle-derived alkaline basalt carried the sapphire... to the surface during ~4–3 Ma.' Related: Fanka et al. 2021, J. Earth Sci. 32:1035-1052 (doi:10.1007/s12583-020-1347-1; zircon U–Pb of felsic xenoliths in the Bo Phloi basalt). That DOI is verified but I could not access the abstract, so I did not use it.

title_th: อายุคาร์บอน-14 ของกรวดไพลินบ่อพลอย
title_en: Radiocarbon ages of Bo Phloi sapphire gravels
finding_th: ไพลินที่บ่อพลอยสะสมตัวในชั้นกรวดของที่ราบน้ำท่วมถึงและตะพักลำน้ำระดับต่ำ การหาอายุด้วยคาร์บอน-14 (radiocarbon, 14C) ของเศษไม้และพีต (peat) ในชั้นที่มีอัญมณีชี้ว่าตะกอนชุดนี้สะสมตัวในสมัยไพลสโตซีนตอนกลางถึงตอนปลาย
finding_en: At Bo Phloi, sapphires are concentrated in gravel beds of floodplain and low-terrace deposits. Radiocarbon (14C) dating of wood and peat within the gem-bearing layers shows that the deposit formed in the middle to late Pleistocene.
value: 14C on wood/peat: middle–late Pleistocene

citation.text: Choowong 2002, Quaternary geology and sapphire deposits from the Bo Phloi gem field, Kanchanaburi Province, Western Thailand, Journal of Asian Earth Sciences 20:119–125

_notes: DOI confirmed on Crossref (J. Asian Earth Sci. 20(2):119-125, Jan 2002). ScienceDirect, ADS, ResearchGate and Academia were all blocked, so I read only search-engine snippets of the abstract: 'Gemstones are recognized in floodplain and low terrace deposits where gemstone paystreaks concentrate mostly inside layers of gravel beds and foreset-bedded gravels lithofacies. C-14 dating of wood and peat within gemstone-bearing layers indicated that the deposit formed during the middle to late Pleistocene.' One snippet also gave numbers ('woods... dated by 14C... mostly between 24,500 and 33,500 yrs BP'), but I could not tie them to this paper, so they are NOT in 'value'; check them. Note: finite 14C ages of 24–34 ka would be late Pleistocene and are near the method's limit, so 'middle Pleistocene' cannot come from 14C. Check whether luminescence was also used. The timeline age of 0.393 Ma for 'sapphire-gravels' has no support in this source. Sutthirat et al. 2020 detrital-zircon ages (4.4 and 10.86 Ma) give only a maximum age for the gravels.

title_th: อายุคาร์บอน-14 ของแหล่งโบราณคดีบ้านเก่า
title_en: Radiocarbon dating of Ban Kao Neolithic
finding_th: ค่าอายุคาร์บอน-14 (radiocarbon, 14C) จากถ่านไม้ในชั้นสมัยหินใหม่ (Neolithic) ทั้งสองระยะของแหล่งฝังศพบ้านเก่า จังหวัดกาญจนบุรี ซึ่งขุดค้นโดยคณะสำรวจไทย–เดนมาร์กช่วงต้นทศวรรษ 1960 ชี้ว่าชุมชนตั้งถิ่นฐานในช่วงครึ่งแรกของสหัสวรรษที่ 2 ก่อนคริสตกาล หรือช้ากว่านั้นเล็กน้อย (ราว 4,000–3,500 ปีก่อน)
finding_en: Charcoal radiocarbon dates from both Neolithic phases at the Ban Kao settlement and cemetery, excavated by the Thai–Danish expedition in the early 1960s, place occupation in the first half of the 2nd millennium BC or slightly later (about 4000–3500 years ago).
value: Charcoal 14C: first half of 2nd millennium BC or slightly later

citation.text: Higham, Higham, Ciarla, Douka, Kijngam & Rispoli 2011, The origins of the Bronze Age of Southeast Asia, Journal of World Prehistory 24:227–274

_notes: DOI confirmed on Crossref (J. World Prehist. 24:227-274, Dec 2011). Read the FULL TEXT (PDF hosted at pages.upd.edu.ph). Exact statement (p. 244): 'Ban Kao is a Neolithic settlement and cemetery in Kanchanaburi, excavated in the early 1960s by Sørensen (Sørensen and Hatting 1967), who obtained radiocarbon determinations relating to both the Neolithic phases. These indicate settlement within the first half of the 2nd millennium BC or slightly later (Fig. 8).' The caption of Fig. 8 says the dates are 'based on charcoal'. The paper does not list lab numbers or BP values in the text; these are in Sørensen & Hatting 1967, Archaeological Excavations in Thailand vol. II: Ban-Kao (Munksgaard), which I did not see. A search summary claimed a Bayesian re-analysis (occupation from the 19th/18th century BC, lasting about five centuries), but I could NOT find its source, so it is not used. The '4000–3500 years ago' in the finding is my conversion of '1st half of 2nd millennium BC'. Charcoal may have inbuilt age, so the dates may be slightly too old. Site is null: Wikipedia gives 13.867 N, 99.150 E for Ban Kao, but I did not confirm that this is the excavation site.
